title: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2610.27047v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: EHR foundation models promise scalable clinical prediction across health systems, yet their deployment is constrained by a tokenization bottleneck. The same clinical concept can appear as different ontology codes, local identifiers, synonyms, or free-text descriptions, which standard EHR tokenizers treat as unrelated symbols. A model trained on MIMIC-III with a closed-vocabulary tokenizer can use only 13% of eICU events. We introduce MEDIATOR, a discrete ontology-agnostic tokenizer that maps any clinical concept expressed as text into a shared vector-quantized codebook, turning EHR harmonization into open-vocabulary tokenization without manual mappings or a fixed vocabulary. Trained with synonym supervision and guided by enriched concept descriptions, code co-occurrence, and relation graphs, MEDIATOR collapses equivalent expressions while organizing distinct concepts in a medically meaningful discrete space. Used as the token interface

translated_title: 面向本体无关电子健康记录建模的离散神经中介语言
translated_abstract: 电子健康记录（EHR）基础模型有望实现跨医疗系统的可扩展临床预测，但其部署受到分词瓶颈的制约。同一临床概念可能以不同的本体编码、本地标识符、同义词或自由文本描述的形式出现，而标准的EHR分词器会将它们视为互不相关的符号。使用封闭词表分词器在MIMIC-III上训练的模型，仅能使用eICU中13%的事件。我们提出了MEDIATOR，这是一种离散的、本体无关的分词器，它将任何以文本形式表达的临床概念映射到一个共享的向量量化码本中，从而将EHR数据协调统一转化为开放词表分词问题，无需人工映射或固定词表。通过同义词监督进行训练，并借助丰富的概念描述、编码共现信息和关系图进行引导，MEDIATOR能够合并等价表达，同时在具有医学意义的离散空间中组织不同概念。用作分词接口时（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出MEDIATOR——一种本体无关的离散分词器，通过将任意文本形式表达的临床概念映射到共享的向量量化码本，将EHR数据协调转化为开放词表分词问题，从而打破不同医疗系统间的编码壁垒。
en_tdlr: MEDIATOR is a discrete ontology-agnostic tokenizer that maps any text-expressed clinical concept into a shared vector-quantized codebook, turning EHR harmonization into open-vocabulary tokenization to overcome the cross-system vocabulary bottleneck in clinical foundation models.
